#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <cuda.h>

#include "binomialOptions.h"
#include "realtype.h"


//Preprocessed input option data
typedef struct
{
  real S;
  real X;
  real vDt;
  real puByDf;
  real pdByDf;
} __TOptionData;


// Overloaded shortcut functions for different precision modes
#ifndef DOUBLE_PRECISION
__device__ inline float expiryCallValue(float S, float X, float vDt, int i)
{
  float d = S * __expf(vDt * (2.0f * i - NUM_STEPS)) - X;
  return (d > 0.0F) ? d : 0.0F;
}
#else
__device__ inline double expiryCallValue(double S, double X, double vDt, int i)
{
  double d = S * exp(vDt * (2.0 * i - NUM_STEPS)) - X;
  return (d > 0.0) ? d : 0.0;
}
#endif


// GPU kernel
#define THREADBLOCK_SIZE 128
#define ELEMS_PER_THREAD (NUM_STEPS/THREADBLOCK_SIZE)
#if NUM_STEPS % THREADBLOCK_SIZE
#error Bad constants
#endif

__global__ void binomialOptionsKernel(const __TOptionData *__restrict d_OptionData,
                                      real *__restrict d_CallValue)
{
  __shared__ real call_exchange[THREADBLOCK_SIZE + 1];

  const int     tid = threadIdx.x;
  const real      S = d_OptionData[blockIdx.x].S;
  const real      X = d_OptionData[blockIdx.x].X;
  const real    vDt = d_OptionData[blockIdx.x].vDt;
  const real puByDf = d_OptionData[blockIdx.x].puByDf;
  const real pdByDf = d_OptionData[blockIdx.x].pdByDf;

  real call[ELEMS_PER_THREAD + 1];
#pragma unroll
  for(int i = 0; i < ELEMS_PER_THREAD; ++i)
    call[i] = expiryCallValue(S, X, vDt, tid * ELEMS_PER_THREAD + i);

  if (tid == 0)
    call_exchange[THREADBLOCK_SIZE] = expiryCallValue(S, X, vDt, NUM_STEPS);

  int final_it = max(0, tid * ELEMS_PER_THREAD - 1);

#pragma unroll 16
  for(int i = NUM_STEPS; i > 0; --i)
  {
    call_exchange[tid] = call[0];
    __syncthreads();
    call[ELEMS_PER_THREAD] = call_exchange[tid + 1];
    __syncthreads();

    if (i > final_it)
    {
#pragma unroll
      for(int j = 0; j < ELEMS_PER_THREAD; ++j)
        call[j] = puByDf * call[j + 1] + pdByDf * call[j];
    }
  }

  if (tid == 0)
  {
    d_CallValue[blockIdx.x] = call[0];
  }
}

// Host-side interface to GPU binomialOptions
extern "C" void binomialOptionsGPU(
    real *callValue,
    TOptionData  *optionData,
    int optN,
    int numIterations
    )
{
  __TOptionData h_OptionData[MAX_OPTIONS];

  for (int i = 0; i < optN; i++)
  {
    const real      T = optionData[i].T;
    const real      R = optionData[i].R;
    const real      V = optionData[i].V;

    const real     dt = T / (real)NUM_STEPS;
    const real    vDt = V * sqrt(dt);
    const real    rDt = R * dt;
    //Per-step interest and discount factors
    const real     If = exp(rDt);
    const real     Df = exp(-rDt);
    //Values and pseudoprobabilities of upward and downward moves
    const real      u = exp(vDt);
    const real      d = exp(-vDt);
    const real     pu = (If - d) / (u - d);
    const real     pd = (real)1.0 - pu;
    const real puByDf = pu * Df;
    const real pdByDf = pd * Df;

    h_OptionData[i].S      = (real)optionData[i].S;
    h_OptionData[i].X      = (real)optionData[i].X;
    h_OptionData[i].vDt    = (real)vDt;
    h_OptionData[i].puByDf = (real)puByDf;
    h_OptionData[i].pdByDf = (real)pdByDf;
  }

  __TOptionData *d_OptionData;
  cudaMalloc ((void**)&d_OptionData, sizeof(__TOptionData) * MAX_OPTIONS);
  cudaMemcpy(d_OptionData, h_OptionData, optN * sizeof(__TOptionData), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  real *d_CallValue;
  cudaMalloc ((void**)&d_CallValue, sizeof(real) * MAX_OPTIONS);

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < numIterations; i++)
    binomialOptionsKernel<<<optN, THREADBLOCK_SIZE>>>(d_OptionData, d_CallValue);

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average kernel execution time : %f (us)\n", time * 1e-3f / numIterations);

  cudaMemcpy(callValue, d_CallValue, optN *sizeof(real), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
  cudaFree(d_OptionData);
  cudaFree(d_CallValue);
}

// Helper function, returning uniformly distributed

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{

    callValueBS[MAX_OPTIONS],

    sumDelta, sumRef, gpuTime, errorVal;

  printf("Generating input data...\n");

#include <stdio.h>
#include <math.h>
#include "binomialOptions.h"
#include "realtype.h"

// Polynomial approximation of cumulative normal distribution function
static real CND(real d)
{
  const real       A1 = 0.31938153;
  const real       A2 = -0.356563782;
  const real       A3 = 1.781477937;
  const real       A4 = -1.821255978;
  const real       A5 = 1.330274429;
  const real RSQRT2PI = 0.39894228040143267793994605993438;

  real
    K = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.2316419 * fabs(d));

  real
    cnd = RSQRT2PI * exp(- 0.5 * d * d) *
    (K * (A1 + K * (A2 + K * (A3 + K * (A4 + K * A5)))));

  if (d > 0)
    cnd = 1.0 - cnd;

  return cnd;
}

extern "C" void BlackScholesCall(
    real &callResult,
    TOptionData optionData
    )
{
  real S = optionData.S;
  real X = optionData.X;
  real T = optionData.T;
  real R = optionData.R;
  real V = optionData.V;

  real sqrtT = sqrt(T);
  real    d1 = (log(S / X) + (R + (real)0.5 * V * V) * T) / (V * sqrtT);
  real    d2 = d1 - V * sqrtT;
  real CNDD1 = CND(d1);
  real CNDD2 = CND(d2);

  //Calculate Call and Put simultaneously
  real expRT = exp(- R * T);
  callResult   = (real)(S * CNDD1 - X * expRT * CNDD2);
}

// Process an array of OptN options on CPU
// Note that CPU code is for correctness testing only and not for benchmarking.
static real expiryCallValue(real S, real X, real vDt, int i)
{
  real d = S * exp(vDt * (real)(2 * i - NUM_STEPS)) - X;
  return (d > (real)0) ? d : (real)0;
}

extern "C" void binomialOptionsCPU(
    real &callResult,
    TOptionData optionData
    )
{
  static real Call[NUM_STEPS + 1];

  const real       S = optionData.S;
  const real       X = optionData.X;
  const real       T = optionData.T;
  const real       R = optionData.R;
  const real       V = optionData.V;

  const real      dt = T / (real)NUM_STEPS;
  const real     vDt = V * sqrt(dt);
  const real     rDt = R * dt;
  //Per-step interest and discount factors
  const real      If = exp(rDt);
  const real      Df = exp(-rDt);
  //Values and pseudoprobabilities of upward and downward moves
  const real       u = exp(vDt);
  const real       d = exp(-vDt);
  const real      pu = (If - d) / (u - d);
  const real      pd = 1.0 - pu;
  const real  puByDf = pu * Df;
  const real  pdByDf = pd * Df;

  // Compute values at expiration date:
  // call option value at period end is V(T) = S(T) - X
  // if S(T) is greater than X, or zero otherwise.
  // The computation is similar for put options.
  for (int i = 0; i <= NUM_STEPS; i++)
    Call[i] = expiryCallValue(S, X, vDt, i);

  // Walk backwards up binomial tree
  for (int i = NUM_STEPS; i > 0; i--)
    for (int j = 0; j <= i - 1; j++)
      Call[j] = puByDf * Call[j + 1] + pdByDf * Call[j];

  callResult = (real)Call[0];
}

Each thread computes 16 expiryCallValue calls (ELEMS_PER_THREAD = 2048/128 = 16), plus thread 0 computes one extra.

For each expiryCallValue: The SASS shows the pattern of computing `vDt * (2*i - NUM_STEPS)` then `__expf(result)` then `S * exp_result - X` then max(0, result).

Looking at the SASS initialization code (before the main loop at .L_x_32):
- I2FP (int-to-float conversions): 16 per thread
- FFMA for `val * 2.0 - 2048`: 16 per thread → 16 FP32 FLOPs each (2 ops per FFMA) = 32 total... actually FFMA counts as 2 FLOPs (multiply + add).
- FMUL for `R8 * result` (vDt * linear_term): 16+1 per thread (thread 0 gets extra)
- FMUL for `result * 1.4426950216293334961` (log2(e) conversion for EX2): 16+1
- FSETP.GEU (comparison, not a FLOP)
- Conditional FMUL R*0.5 for denorm handling: 16+1
- MUFU.EX2: 16+1 (each is 1 FP32 FLOP)
- Conditional FMUL R*R (squaring for denorm): 16+1
- FFMA for `S * exp_result - X`: 16+1 (2 FLOPs each)
- FMNMX for max(0, result): 16+1 (1 FLOP each)

Wait, let me count more carefully from SASS. The HFMA2.MMA at 0x0090 and 0x0ce0 are FP16 operations.

Per thread init (16 values, ignoring thread 0's extra):
- 16 FFMA (val*2-2048): 16 × 2 = 32 FLOPs
- 16 FMUL (vDt * linear): 16 FLOPs  
- 16 FMUL (× log2e): 16 FLOPs
- 16 FSETP: not FLOPs
- Up to 16 FMUL (×0.5 for denorm, conditional - but for typical values these may or may not execute; conservatively assume they don't for most)
- 16 MUFU.EX2: 16 FLOPs
- Up to 16 FMUL (squaring for denorm, conditional)
- 16 FFMA (S*exp-X): 32 FLOPs
- 16 FMNMX (max): 16 FLOPs

For the normal path (no denorm handling), per thread: 32+16+16+16+32+16 = 128 FP32 FLOPs for 16 values.

Thread 0 extra: +8 FLOPs (1 FMUL + 1 FMUL×log2e + 1 MUFU.EX2 + 1 FFMA(2 ops) + 1 FMNMX + 1 FMUL(vDt*2048) = ~8)

The loop runs from NUM_STEPS=2048 down to 1, so 2048 iterations. The compiler has unrolled by 16 (pragma unroll 16), creating 16 "sub-iterations" per outer loop body, giving 2048/16 = 128 outer iterations.

Each sub-iteration, when the predicate is taken, does 16 FMUL + 16 FFMA + 1 FFMA (for the boundary element using shared memory value) = 16 + 16×2 + 2 = 50 FP32 FLOPs per sub-iteration per thread.

Actually looking at each taken block: 16 FMUL + 16 FFMA = 16 + 32 = 48 FLOPs. Wait, counting from SASS: there are 15 FMUL + 15 FFMA pairs for call[0..14], plus 1 FMUL for call[15] (pdByDf*call[15]), 1 FFMA for call[15] (puByDf*call[16]+prev), and 1 FFMA for call[0] boundary. From .L_x_1 block (0x0e80-0x1070): 16 FMUL + 16 FFMA = 16 + 32 = 48 FP32 FLOPs.

Each thread has final_it = max(0, tid*16 - 1). The condition `i > final_it` determines how many iterations each thread executes. Thread 0: final_it=0, executes all 2048 iterations. Thread k (k>0): final_it = 16k-1, executes iterations from 2048 down to 16k, which is 2048-16k+1 iterations... wait, i > final_it means i > 16k-1, so i >= 16k, giving 2048-16k+1 iterations.

Total FP32 FLOPs in main loop per block = sum over threads of (iterations_executed × 48):
- Thread 0: 2048 × 48
- Thread k (k=1..127): (2048 - 16k + 1) × 48 = (2049 - 16k) × 48

But wait, the unrolling by 16 means each "outer iteration" processes 16 sub-steps. The predicates in SASS check different thresholds. Let me reconsider.

Actually, looking at the SASS structure more carefully: the outer loop at .L_x_32 decrements R6 by 16 each iteration (IADD3 R6, R6, -0x10 at 0x3660). Actually HFMA2.MMA R6, -RZ, RZ, 0, 0.0001220703125 — this is materializing a constant. 0.0001220703125 = 2^(-13). As a bit pattern reinterpreted as int32: 0x39000000. Hmm, that's 2048 as a float... no. Let me reconsider: the HFMA2 at 0x0090 produces R10 = 2.0 (used for the 2*i computation). The HFMA2 at 0x0ce0 produces R6. 0.0001220703125 = 1/8192 = 2^-13. As uint32 bit pattern: 0x39000000. But R6 is used as an integer loop counter. So R6 = 0x39000000? That doesn't make sense for a loop counter of 2048.

Wait — looking at SASS more carefully, R6 is used in integer comparisons (ISETP.GT.U32). The HFMA2.MMA is being used to materialize a constant bit pattern. 0.0001220703125 in IEEE 754 float = 0x39000000. But 2048 as uint32 = 0x00000800. Let me reconsider: HFMA2.MMA R6, -RZ, RZ, 0, 0.0001220703125. The encoding might produce 0x00000800 = 2048 in the register. The disassembler might be showing the immediate as a float interpretation. 0x800 = 2048. So R6 = 2048 initially.

So R6 starts at 2048, decremented by 16 each outer iteration → 128 outer iterations.

Within each outer iteration, there are 16 sub-steps, each guarded by a predicate. The predicates check whether the current sub-step index > final_it (R25).

For thread k: final_it = max(0, 16k - 1). R25 = final_it.

For thread 0: R25 = 0. All 16 sub-steps execute when the loop counter > 0, which is always true (loop runs while R6 > 0, and the sub-steps check various offsets of R6 against R25).

Per iteration: 48 FP32 FLOPs (16 FMUL + 16 FFMA).

Main loop FLOPs per block = 133247 × 48 = 6,395,856.

Init FLOPs per block = 128 × 128 + 8 = 16,392 (approximately).

Total FP32 per block ≈ 6,395,856 + 16,392 = 6,412,248.

Total FP32 = 1024 × 6,412,248 ≈ 6,566,141,952.

Hmm, let me be more precise about the init. Actually the denorm branches (FMUL×0.5 and FMUL squaring) likely don't execute for typical values since vDt*(2i-2048) for reasonable financial parameters will be in normal range. So init per thread = 16×(2+1+1+1+2+1) = 16×8 = 128. Thread 0 extra: 1×8 = 8. Per block: 128×128 + 8 = 16,392.

Total FP32 = 1024 × (6,395,856 + 16,392) = 1024 × 6,412,248 = 6,566,141,952.

With 20-byte structs packed contiguously, this is ceil(20480/128) = 160 cache lines = 20,480 bytes from DRAM.

(1 FP32), then FSETP (1 FP32), conditional FMUL by 0.5 (for some threads), MUFU.EX2 (1 FP32), conditional FMUL squaring (for some threads), then FFMA S*exp_result - X (1 FP32), then FMNMX for max(0,d) (1 FP32).

- FMUL R8*result: 16 FMULs = 16 FP32
- FMUL by 1.4426...: 16 FMULs = 16 FP32
- FSETP: 16 FSETPs = 16 FP32

- FFMA S*exp - X: 16 FFMAs = 32 FP32
- FMNMX (max with 0): 16 = 16 FP32

For the 16 regular elements per thread: each has FFMA + FMUL + FMUL(1.4426) + FSETP + MUFU.EX2 + FFMA + FMNMX = 7 FP32 ops (counting FFMA as 2). Actually FFMA is a fused multiply-add = 2 FLOPs. The loop runs from i=NUM_STEPS=2048 down to 1, so 2048 iterations. The compiler has unrolled by 16 (the outer loop body processes 16 iterations of the original loop). So the outer loop runs 2048/16 = 128 times.

Each unrolled iteration body has 16 FMUL + 16 FFMA = 16 + 32 = 48 FP32 ops per inner iteration. But threads only execute the body when i > final_it. For thread tid, final_it = max(0, tid*16 - 1). For each of the 2048 steps, the number of threads that execute the inner work is: for step i (counting from 2048 down to 1), thread tid executes if i > max(0, tid*16-1). Thread 0 always executes (i>0 always true for i>=1). Thread tid executes step i if i > 16*tid - 1, i.e., i >= 16*tid. So for step i, threads 0..floor(i/16) execute (but capped at 127). Actually for tid>=1: condition is i >= 16*tid, so number of active threads = min(128, floor(i/16)+1). For i=2048: all 128 threads. For i=1: only thread 0.

Per active thread per step: 16 FMUL + 16 FFMA = 16 + 32 = 48 FP32 ops.

For i=1..15: floor(i/16)+1 = 1, so 15*1 = 15
For i=16..31: floor(i/16)+1 = 2, so 16*2 = 32

For i=16*0+1..15: 15*1 = 15
For k=1..126: 16*(k+1)
For i=2033..2048: 16*128 = 2048

= 15 + 130032 + 2048

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Single precision is used because DOUBLE_PRECISION is not defined, so real=float. Per thread, initialization computes ELEMS_PER_THREAD=2048/128=16 expiry values; each expiryCallValue does (2*i-NUM_STEPS) [1 int sub, ignored], float conversion, vDt*term (1 mul), __expf(...) (counted here conservatively as 1 FP32 op at source level), S*exp (1 mul), minus X (1 add/sub): 4 FP32 ops, so 16*4=64 per thread; thread 0 computes one extra expiry value (+4). In the main backward loop over i=2048..1, every thread executes for max(0,tid*16-1)<i; summing active iterations over tid=0..127 gives 139392 active (thread,i) pairs, and each active j-update does puByDf*call[j+1] + pdByDf*call[j] = 2 mul + 1 add = 3 FP32 ops for each of 16 j values, so 48 ops per active pair, totaling 139392*48 = 6690816. Adding initialization 128*64=8192 and the extra thread-0 expiry 4 gives 6699012 FP32 FLOPs. This source-level estimate does not include lower-level helper operations inside __expf that SASS would expand into.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The build does not define DOUBLE_PRECISION, so all kernel arithmetic uses float rather than double. Therefore no FP64 arithmetic is executed in the analyzed kernel invocation.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel uses float (real=float) throughout and there are no half or half2 data types or intrinsics in the source. Without SASS evidence of packed-FP16 materialization instructions, the defensible estimate is zero FP16 FLOPs.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each block handles one option and reads d_OptionData[blockIdx.x].{S,X,vDt,puByDf,pdByDf}; all 128 threads redundantly load these 5 floats from global memory, so raw traffic is 1024 blocks * 128 threads * 5 * 4 B = 2621440 B. The working set for d_OptionData actually copied is only optN*sizeof(__TOptionData)=1024*20 B=20480 B, far smaller than the 40 MB L2, so after compulsory fetches the repeated per-thread/per-block accesses can be served from cache; thus DRAM read is best estimated by the unique footprint of 20,480 B for the first invocation.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Only thread 0 of each block stores one float result to d_CallValue[blockIdx.x], so the unique output footprint is 1024 * 4 B = 4096 B. Because this is tiny relative to the 40 MB L2 and there is no evidence of eviction during the first kernel invocation, these write-back cache lines can remain dirty in L2, so DRAM writes during the invocation are estimated as zero.
